evals.prompt: My Claude Agent SDK agent shows up fine in X-Ray and aws/spans, but when I run `agentcore run eval --runtime-arn ...` every evaluator comes back with errorMessage 'Session span data is incomplete. Span with ID: <id> and name: invoke_agent <name> is missing a corresponding log event'. The I/O summary log is definitely in CloudWatch with the right spanId. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers and diagnoses the log-group-suffix mismatch: the instrumentation writes to /aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/{AGENT_ID} but the eval service queries /aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/{AGENT_ID}-{ENDPOINT}. Recommends changing aws.log.group.names, x-aws-log-group OTLP header, and EMF log_group_name all to the -{ENDPOINT}-suffixed path.
expectations: Response identifies the /runtimes/{AGENT_ID}-{ENDPOINT} vs /runtimes/{AGENT_ID} discrepancy as the root cause
Response names all three places that must be updated (resource attribute, OTLP log header, EMF exporter log_group_name)
Response references the AWS SDK sample from getting-started-on-demand.html or the equivalent agentcore run eval behavior
Response does NOT suggest rewriting tool hooks, I/O summary body format, or span hierarchy (those are already correct in this scenario)

evals.prompt: My Claude agent keeps failing AgentCore evaluations with 'LogEventMissingException: Session span data is incomplete. Span with ID: abc123 and name: tool.word_count is missing a corresponding log event'. The agent has basic OTEL (spans export to aws/spans, invoke_agent has its I/O summary) but something is wrong with the tool spans. Can you fix it?
evals.expected_output: The fix adds per-tool I/O summary emission inside post_tool_use_hook, emitted BEFORE span.end() and tied to the tool span via an explicit span_context=(trace_id, span_id, trace_flags) argument. The _emit_structured_log helper accepts a span_context parameter so per-tool logs carry the tool-span's spanId rather than the current-span's.
expectations: Fix emits a per-tool I/O summary log inside post_tool_use_hook before the tool span is ended
Per-tool log uses the tool span's own (trace_id, span_id, trace_flags) via span_context= instead of trace.get_current_span()
Per-tool log body follows the input-role-tool / output-role-assistant shape from references/structured-logs.md
Fix does NOT put role:tool entries into the invoke_agent-level input.messages (that would cause AgentSpanMappingException)

evals.prompt: I have a vanilla Claude Agent SDK agent with no OTEL at all. It uses an MCP-style tool via create_sdk_mcp_server. I need it to pass all 9 AgentCore built-in evaluators when invoked via `agentcore run eval`. Please add full instrumentation but keep the tools and prompts unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Agent is modified with: Resource carrying aws.service.type='gen_ai_agent', aws.log.group.names with -{ENDPOINT} suffix, cloud.resource_id full ARN; TracerProvider using OTLPAwsSpanExporter + BaggageSpanProcessor; LoggerProvider with two loggers under scopes strands.telemetry.tracer and opentelemetry.instrumentation.botocore.bedrock-runtime; MeterProvider with AwsCloudWatchEmfExporter; pre/post tool-use hooks that create parented tool spans and emit per-tool I/O summaries; invoke_agent + execute_event_loop_cycle + chat + chat<model> span hierarchy; session.id via baggage; provider.shutdown() ordering trace→log→metric.
expectations: aws.log.group.names uses the {AGENT_ID}-{ENDPOINT} suffixed path
cloud.resource_id is the full runtime endpoint ARN (arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:<region>:<acct>:runtime/<id>/endpoint/<name>)
The x-aws-log-group OTLP header matches aws.log.group.names exactly
The EMF exporter's log_group_name matches aws.log.group.names exactly
Tracer scope is 'strands.telemetry.tracer' (not __name__)
Tool spans are created with context=_active_cycle_context so they share the invoke_agent traceId
post_tool_use_hook emits a per-tool I/O summary BEFORE span.end() with tool span's span_context
invoke_agent-level I/O summary is emitted AFTER context.detach of the cycle context
invoke_agent input.messages contains only role:user entries (no role:tool)
LogRecord(...) calls do NOT pass a resource= kwarg
Original @tool decorators, tool functions, create_sdk_mcp_server call, and system prompts are byte-identical to the input file
Shutdown order is provider.shutdown() (traces) → _log_provider.shutdown() → _meter_provider.shutdown()

evals.prompt: I'm building a new Claude Agent SDK customer support agent from scratch with three tools: search_kb, create_ticket, check_status. I want it to pass Bedrock AgentCore evaluations from day 1 when deployed to an AgentCore Runtime endpoint named DEFAULT. Set up the observability instrumentation.
evals.expected_output: Produces either a new agent file or a shared _instrumentation.py module plus an agent that imports it, applying every pattern from SKILL.md Steps 1–11. Hook registration covers all three tools. gen_ai.agent.tools attribute lists search_kb/create_ticket/check_status. Instrumentation is cleanly separated from application logic (ideally in a shared module).
expectations: Resource attributes include aws.service.type='gen_ai_agent', aws.log.group.names with -DEFAULT suffix, and cloud.resource_id with endpoint/DEFAULT
gen_ai.agent.tools attribute on invoke_agent span is a JSON array containing all three tool names
PreToolUse and PostToolUse hooks are registered for each tool (HookMatcher wrapped)
All three providers (trace, log, meter) are initialized before the client runs
Shutdown block calls provider.shutdown() BEFORE _log_provider.shutdown() and _meter_provider.shutdown()
Instrumentation does not hardcode the account id or region — sourced from env or botocore session

evals.prompt: I applied the ac-evaluation-transform skill to my agent. Before I run `agentcore run eval`, how do I sanity-check that the telemetry is actually correct in CloudWatch? Give me a checklist.
evals.expected_output: Step-by-step verification: (1) run the agent with a recorded session-id; (2) wait ~4 minutes for CloudWatch ingestion; (3) list streams in /aws/.../runtimes/<id>-<endpoint> and confirm runtime-logs stream exists; (4) Logs Insights filter by session.id, confirm at least one strands.telemetry.tracer record with body.input/body.output/body.usage and per-tool records; (5) query aws/spans for invoke_agent <name> span and match its spanId with the I/O summary spanId; (6) run `agentcore run eval --runtime-arn <arn> --session-id <sid>` only after the span↔log spanId correspondence is confirmed.
expectations: Recommends a concrete Logs Insights query that filters on attributes.session.id
Recommends an aws/spans query that finds 'invoke_agent <name>' by name
Explicitly checks that the invoke_agent spanId appears in both the span record and the I/O summary log record
Mentions the ~4-minute CloudWatch ingestion delay
Uses the -{ENDPOINT}-suffixed log group path (not the bare /runtimes/<id> path)
